questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I knew a little about Korea from popculture and an interest in food. I've traveled extensively in Asia and never got to visit Korea. I wanted to go to a place that was radically different to Denmark

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Due to covid there were no intro programs, no physical class and a lot of restrictions this had a big impact on the stay

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. I do however think that SKKU was horrible at communicating what needed to be know

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: My landlord helped me with a lot of stuff. Simple Spaces highly recommend it!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Mentioned earlier, but communication is really bad. They cancelled the buddy program despite it still going on at every other uni.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Kind of hard. I stayed at Simples Spaces. Highly recommend

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Do live off campus. I heard from people living on campus that rules are ridiculous and limiting.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Do not live on campus

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was given a course catalog from a previous year in which there were 22 course in my Major taught in English, however when I had to registere only 7 course were available 2 of which are Masters courses. None of the course I had initially wanted was there, so I ended up having to take stuff I did not want. Had I known this I would've chosen another uni.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Fastest get the course.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Group chat and email correspondence

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the ones I wanted, however as mentioned catalog was nothing like promised

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Pick another uni, heard good things about Yonsei, SNU and KU. At Yonsei you only need 9 credits compared to 12-15 at most other institutions.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had one course where the teacher barely spoke legible English.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Level was about the same as Copenhagen University.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I feel that at KU its more about learning. In Korea all of the focus is on memorisation. If you can remember everything as it is written you will get good grades, however there is no focus on actual learning. Free though and discussion is not encouraged as it is here.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Brain Science
Plant Physiology
Micro Biology
Evolution

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Brain Science was good. Competent teacher, interesting subject.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Food in the supermarked is very expensive and selection is bad unless you live near a hypermarket.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food In general was more expensive. Alcohol (soju) is dirt cheap so is cigarettes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Everything closed due to covid

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Non

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to Seoraksan, juju island, Busan. A lot of mountains to climb if you're into that.
Museums, markets etc. Seoul has so much to do.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I have no tips as I only saw other local students when I had exams

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Korea is a snitch society. People will not ask you to turn the sound down etc, they will just call the police. There is no trust among strangers.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Loved how accessible it is to eat out.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Pick another one
2. Be aware its in Suwon, 1 hour+ from Seoul
3. 1.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: They will not fail you. Everybody passes.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Loved getting to live in a foreign culture for a while, and of course the friends I gained.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing friends, foods etc from home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: This review may paint Korea in a bad light. However I overall had a great experience, there are som major negatives, but overall I enjoyed it, its a beautiful country with a lot to offer though I would recommend Japan for a similar possibly better experience. And do not go to SKKU Suwon campus it is far.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
